evidence.title: Complex paths around the sign problem (Rev. Mod. Phys. 94, 015006)
evidence.supports: Direct: abstract of the authoritative 2022 Reviews of Modern Physics review inspected. It presents the sign problem as the standing obstacle that makes dense matter, the doped repulsive Hubbard model, and real-time observables inaccessible to Monte Carlo 'as it currently stands', and reviews thimble/complex-path methods as partial attacks with successes limited to specific examples — i.e., the general problem is treated as open, not solved.

evidence.title: Sign Problem in Quantum Monte Carlo Simulation (Encyclopedia of Condensed Matter Physics, 2nd ed., 2024)
evidence.supports: Direct: abstract of the 2024 encyclopedia chapter by Pan and Meng inspected. It surveys efforts to 'cure, ease and even make use of' the sign problem — symmetry analysis, basis optimization, algebraic-sign regimes — all explicitly model- or basis-dependent, confirming that no generic polynomial-cost solution exists and that progress consists of special-case circumventions rather than a general answer.

evidence.title: Computational Complexity and Fundamental Limitations to Fermionic Quantum Monte Carlo Simulations (Phys. Rev. Lett. 94, 170201)
evidence.supports: Direct: abstract of Troyer and Wiese inspected; it is the authoritative formulation of the named problem and supplies the standing rigorous result — the sign problem is NP-hard in general, so a generic polynomial solution would imply P = NP. This remains the best result on the question and bounds rather than settles the equilibrium Monte Carlo existence question.

evidence.title: A Generic Solution of Fermion Sign Problem
evidence.supports: Contested claim: preprint by Wang and Sun claims the sign problem is 'completely solved' via positive-weight path replacement, applied to the 2D Hubbard model. It remains unrefereed (v6, May 2022), is not cited as a resolution in the subsequent review literature (including the 2024 Pan-Meng chapter, which continues to treat the problem as unsolved), and resembles basis-reformulation approaches known not to yield generic polynomial cost. Recorded so the claim is visible; it cannot be counted as closure.

evidence.title: Quantum critical points and the sign problem (Science 375, 418)
evidence.supports: Supplementary: Mondaini, Tarat, and Scalettar connect the sign problem to quantum critical phenomena, treating it as a fundamental physical property of the model rather than a removable artifact; cited in 2025-2026 literature alongside Troyer-Wiese. Metadata level only — included as context that current research continues to investigate, not resolve, the sign problem.
